result:
I checked what's actually in this worktree before touching anything, and the ask can't be done yet — here's why, and what I found instead.

**What's missing.** The world tint isn't a real switch in the game yet. `systems/look_lab.gd` only has three axes today (cot look, station discovery, already-done reply) — no tint axis, no colour grade. That work belongs to a separate item already queued to Jade ("Make the world's colour a real switch in the game"), and it hasn't run. My worktree is a snapshot of the game as it ships today, with nothing to pin the visual test to and no new pixels to bake into a baseline. "Refresh the baseline in the same change that adds the tint" only makes sense as one change owned by whoever writes the tint — I can't fake that from the outside without guessing at Jade's implementation.

**What I did check.** The visual regression harness (`tools/test_visuals.gd`) has no hook for `LookLab` at all right now — it resets the HUD debug readout and the build-version stamp before capturing, but nothing about look-axis state. That's fine today because the three existing axes default to the values the baseline was shot with, so nothing drifts by accident. It means the seam this item wants — an explicit pin — doesn't exist yet either; it has to be added alongside whatever Jade names the new axis, not invented ahead of it.

**One thing worth flagging to Jade directly:** `main.gd` already has a variable called `world_tint` — that's the existing day/night `CanvasModulate` (T-14/Q-38), unrelated to the new look-axis idea. Same words, different feature. Worth Jade picking a name for the new axis that doesn't collide with that in code or in conversation.

**Blocked on:** Jade's item landing first. Once the tint axis exists in the shared tree, I can pin the test to its shipping value and regenerate `tools/baseline.png` in one pass — that's a fast follow, not a redesign.

Nothing changed in the working tree this session.
